message.content:
Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) is the dominant, cost-optimized chemistry for residential energy storage in 2026, while solid-state batteries (SSBs) represent an emerging, high-growth paradigm still in early commercialization. According to `battery_one_research.md`, LFP residential system cells cost approximately $60 to $80 per kWh, with fully installed systems ranging from $300 to $600 per kWh, and offer a proven lifespan of 4,000 to 6,000+ cycles with 89% to 94% round-trip efficiency. In contrast, `battery_two_research.md` notes that solid-state batteries lack broad retail price benchmarks and remain expensive due to complex manufacturing, though the global SSB market is projected to scale rapidly from billions in the mid-2020s toward the mid-2030s.

While the team successfully aligned on comparison metrics—such as energy density, safety, cost maturity, and cycle life—as documented in `team_discussion_summary.md`, the final comparison report (step s4) failed to execute and produced nothing. Consequently, a synthesized, side-by-side evaluation combining all researched metrics into a final deliverable is currently missing.
